newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - LVMH confirms 11 pct GrandMet stake.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - LVMH confirms 11 pct GrandMet stake.

text.p: LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton confirmed on Wednesday that it raised its stake in Britain's Grand Metropolitan to 11.05 percent, increasing pressure on partners GrandMet and Guinness to agree to a three-way drinks merger.

LVMH paid for the 4.6 percent holding, which cost roughly six billion francs, largely by selling Guinness shares, cutting its stake in the Anglo-Irish group to 12.5 percent from 14.2 percent, dealers said.

Share analysts said LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault was traveling to London on Thursday to drum up support from institutional investors in the British companies for his plan in the event a deal cannot be struck among the three chairmen.
He can block the deal outright if he can form an investor alliance representing at least 25 percent of GrandMet's capital.
Analysts said LVMH may buy more GrandMet shares if Arnault does not line up enough support for his alternative plan on Thursday.

Guinness's board met on Wednesday and accepted Arnault's resignation, tendered earlier in the week, but did not comment on his proposed alternative to its own plan, announced in May, to merge with GrandMet into a 24 billion stg ($40.3 billion) drinks, brewing and food group.
Guinness said no deadline had been set for any announcement. Observers said the British companies may reply this week or next.
"They need time. They're working out their calculations and they're watching to see what else he has in his arsenal," one Paris-based analyst said.
Shares in GrandMet fell 7-1/2 pence on Wednesday to 613 and Guinness's stock fell 6-1/2 pence to 598-3/4.
Shares in LVMH rose 4.3 percent to 1,626 francs as investors bet on what looks to be Arnault's battle plan.
"I think Arnault has the upper hand and the market's pricing that in. Guinness and Grand Met are on the defensive," said an analyst in London.
"Arnault's coming to London tomorrow to see large institutional investors in Guinness and GrandMet."

He is expected to press his point that a three-way drinks group of top brands like Moet & Chandon, Johnnie Walker, Gilbey's, J&B and Hennessy cognacs will create more shareholder value than a sprawling fast food-to-drinks conglomerate.

"Bernard Arnault's strategy is to hold 10 percent of Guinness and 10 percent of GrandMet, a level which permits him to call extraordinary general meetings under British law," Paris brokerage Ferri said.
Arnault signalled recently that he was flexible on a key point -- what stake he envisages for LVMH in the new drinks group.
LVMH initially said its 66 percent Moet Hennessy stake and its holdings in Guinness and GrandMet would entitle it to 35 percent.
The British companies have said LVMH's holdings would leave it with 25 percent and a compromise around 30 percent looks likely.
"They'll meet halfway," the London analyst forecast.

Analysts say LVMH, the largest shareholder in both Guinness and GrandMet, opposes their merger plan because it risks marginalising its Moet Hennessy drinks business and locking up part of the group's capital in a subsidiary of the new merged group.
-- Paris Newsroom, +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 0.595 British Pounds)
